info.name: Budgeteer — Transaction Sync
info.description:
Manual testing collection for Phase 4: Monzo Transaction Sync.

## Recommended Order

1. **Setup** — Quick Login + verify Monzo is connected
2. **Inspect DB** — confirm tables are empty
3. **Trigger Sync** — use dev trigger to run backfill without re-doing OAuth
4. **Verify Results** — check accounts and transactions were created
5. **Delta Sync** — trigger delta and confirm only new rows are added
6. **Edge Cases** — unauthenticated, no connection, etc.

## Prerequisites
- App running with `dev` profile (`./scripts/dev.sh start`)
- Monzo OAuth already completed (you have an active connection)
- Import `budgeteer-local.postman_environment.json` and select it
- Run `⚡ Quick Login` first to set auth cookies

## What This Tests
- POST /api/test/auth/sync/trigger (backfill)
- GET /api/monzo/status (tokenStatus field)
- Database state via curl-accessible psql

item.name: 2. Trigger Backfill

exec: console.warn("⚠️  access_token not set — run Quick Login first");
console.log("✅ Backfill complete — run DB queries to verify:");
console.log("  SELECT id, account_type, last_transaction_id, last_synced_at FROM monzo_accounts;");

request.description:
Triggers a full backfill for the authenticated user's active Monzo connection.

**How it works without re-doing OAuth:**
1. Your Monzo tokens are stored encrypted in `monzo_connections`
2. The `MonzoTokenRefreshJob` keeps them alive automatically
3. This endpoint finds your active connection by `userId` and calls `backfill()` directly
4. `backfill()` decrypts the token, calls `GET /accounts` then `GET /transactions` per account
5. All data is upserted into `monzo_accounts` and `monzo_transactions`

**Note:** Unlike post-OAuth backfill (which is async), this endpoint runs **synchronously** — the response waits for full completion.

**Expected response:**
```json
{"success": true, "data": null}
```

After success, check:
- `monzo_accounts` has rows with your real account IDs
- `monzo_transactions` has your real transactions
- `last_transaction_id` is set on each account (cursor for next delta)
- `last_synced_at` is set

⚠️ Dev profile only.

item.name: 4. Idempotency (Re-run Backfill)

exec: console.log("Now verify row counts are UNCHANGED vs the first run:");
console.log("Check that updated_at did NOT change for existing rows");
console.log("(upsert only updates mutable fields like settled_at / amount)");

request.description:
Run backfill a second time without resetting DB.

**What to verify:**
- Row counts in `monzo_accounts` and `monzo_transactions` are IDENTICAL to after the first run
- `last_synced_at` on accounts updates (expected — we always record sync time)
- `last_transaction_id` cursor does NOT change (same latest transaction)
- No duplicate transactions

This proves the native upsert (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`) is working correctly.

item.description: Run backfill twice and confirm row counts don't change — verifies the upsert is idempotent.

item.name: 5. Edge Cases

exec: console.log("✅ Token is valid — sync should work fine");
console.log("⚠️  Token expiring soon — refresh job will run shortly");
console.log("❌ Token EXPIRED — sync will fail, trigger a refresh or re-connect");
console.log("❌ Token REVOKED — user denied access in Monzo app, re-connect needed");

request.description:
Inspect the `tokenStatus` field to understand token health.

Possible values:
- `VALID` — token is fresh, sync will work
- `EXPIRING_SOON` — within the refresh threshold, job will renew it shortly
- `EXPIRED` — token expired, sync will attempt eager refresh on next call
- `REVOKED` — user revoked access in Monzo app, re-OAuth required
- `UNKNOWN` — no token / never connected
